findings.claim: The current explain() function has the signature `def explain(decision: Decision) -> str` and only reads decision.outcome and decision.rule_results; it does not accept or reference any risk profile or risk band data.

The production call site of explain() is in demo-repo/src/loanflow/cli.py's _cmd_decide function, called as `explain(result.decision)`, where `result` is the object returned by run_pipeline(); no risk profile data is passed to explain() at this call site today.
There is no call site of explain() anywhere in the repository other than the one production call in cli.py and the three test calls in test_explanations.py.

search_attempts.result: Matches found only in demo-repo/src/loanflow/cli.py:67 (call), demo-repo/src/loanflow/explanations.py:20 (definition), and demo-repo/tests/unit/test_explanations.py:10,20,29 (test calls). No other files in the repository call explain().

findings.claim: demo-repo/tests/unit/test_explanations.py currently contains exactly three tests (approve, refer, decline), each of which constructs a Decision with exactly two positional arguments (outcome, a tuple of RuleResult) and none of which reference a risk band.

findings.claim: None of the three in-scope files (explanations.py, cli.py, test_explanations.py) contain any reference to 'risk' (case-insensitive) in their current state.

Under the current code, explain() has no existing data channel through which a risk band value could reach the explanation text: its only parameter is a Decision, and Decision itself is constructed today with exactly two positional fields (outcome, rule_results) with nothing else.
findings.reasoning: F-1 shows explain()'s current signature takes only a `decision: Decision` parameter and its body reads only decision.outcome and decision.rule_results. F-4 shows that, in every existing construction of Decision (across all three current tests), exactly two positional arguments are supplied with no risk-profile-related field. Combining these, neither explain()'s parameter list nor the Decision object it receives currently carries risk band data, so satisfying AC-1 will require the risk band to reach explain() through some channel that does not exist in the code today.

open_questions: AC-1 asserts the access pattern PipelineResult.risk_profile.overall_band.value, but pipeline.py, risk_profile.py, decisions.py, and risk_bands.py are all listed as out_of_scope for this research task, so the exact attribute names, the overall_band field's type, and .value semantics could not be independently verified against executable code. A repo-wide grep for 'overall_band' did surface demo-repo/src/loanflow/risk_profile.py and demo-repo/tests/unit/test_risk_profile.py as files referencing it, but per the scope boundary their contents were not opened or cited.
